handoff.purpose: Defines parameter extraction, alias records, and _TypeWalk class with recursive descent over statements.

symbols.name: positional
symbols.note: Local variable in outer scope (likely in a function) built from posonly and args.args.

symbols.name: first_default
symbols.note: Index from which parameters have defaults; computed as len(positional) - len(args.defaults).

symbols.name: _alias_records
symbols.note: Extracts AliasImport records from ast.Import or ast.ImportFrom nodes.

symbols.name: _end_line
symbols.note: Returns the end line number of a node, defaulting to start line if end_lineno missing.

symbols.name: _qual
symbols.note: Joins a tuple of parts and a name with dots.

symbols.name: _TypeWalk
symbols.note: Recursive descent over statements to collect type, field, signature, and alias declarations.

symbols.name: _TypeWalk.__init__
symbols.note: Initializes instance with module name and empty lists for declarations.

symbols.name: _TypeWalk._class
symbols.note: Processes a ClassDef node, appends TypeDecl, and recursively visits body.

symbols.name: _TypeWalk._function
symbols.note: Processes a FunctionDef/AsyncFunctionDef node, appends SignatureDecl, and recursively visits body.

symbols.name: _TypeWalk._self_target
symbols.note: Extracts attribute name from a self-receiver assignment target.

symbols.name: _TypeWalk._annassign
symbols.note: Processes an annotated assignment node (e.g., self.x: int = ...) to record field declarations.

claims.text: ``ast.walk`` cannot be used here: it is breadth-first and exposes no parent link, so ``Outer.Inner`` and ``Cls.method`` are not reconstructible from it.
claims.why: The code implements its own recursive descent with explicit parts tuple to reconstruct qualified names, consistent with the claim.

claims.text: Expressions are never descended into -- no declaration can hide inside one -- which keeps the recursion as shallow as the source's statement nesting.
claims.why: The chunk only shows _class, _function, _annassign methods; no evidence that expressions are skipped, but also no evidence of descending into expressions. The claim is about the overall design, not checkable from this chunk alone.

claims.text: A receiver exists only for a method that actually takes one. Reading the first parameter's real name (rather than assuming "self") keeps a renamed receiver out of the coverage denominator and keeps a staticmethod's first argument IN it.
claims.why: The claim refers to _params_of function which is not defined in this chunk. The logic of bound = receiver if (owner and not is_static and receiver) else "" is present but depends on _params_of returning the correct receiver.

claims.text: Inside a function body: nested defs/classes are in a ``<locals>`` scope, and ``self.x = ...`` assignments belong to the enclosing TYPE.
claims.why: The code passes (*parts, node.name, "<locals>") as parts for recursive visit and passes owner and owner_kind unchanged, consistent with the claim.

observations.what: The code uses 'positional[0].arg' after building positional list; if positional is empty (e.g., function with no parameters except vararg/kwarg), this will raise IndexError.
observations.where: line after for loop returning tuple(out), (positional[0].arg if positional else "")

observations.what: In _annassign, the method signature includes parameters owner, owner_kind, receiver, in_class_body but the chunk does not show how it uses them to record FieldDecl.
The _TypeWalk class initializes 'truncated' to False but never sets it to True within this chunk; it may be set elsewhere or be dead code.
